sentences.text: Complaint is lodged by respondent No.2 based on which a case in Crime No.61/2022 was registered at Kalaburagi City Women Police Station against accused Nos.1 to 7 for offences punishable under Section 498A, 323, 324, 355, 504, 506, 109 r/w 34 of IPC.
On completion of investigation, police have filed the charge sheet.

3. It is alleged that marriage of respondent No.2 was performed with accused No.1 about 7-8 years prior and at the time of marriage gold ornaments, two wheeler and other household articles were given.

She was looked after properly for about four years and thereafter, all the NC:
2024:KHC-K:8412 accused started subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty demanding dowry etc.
4. Petitioner in criminal petition No.200539/2023 is accused No.7 and petitioners in criminal petition No.200541/2023 are accused Nos.2 and 6 respectively.

5. A joint memo has been filed signed by learned counsels appearing for both the parties as well as respondent No.2/defacto complainant, wherein it is stated that the dispute has been settled and both accused No.1 and respondent No.2 are living happily as husband and wife.
Both the parties have requested to quash the proceedings, to protect the institution of marriage.
6. Respondent No.2/defacto complainant as well as her husband are present before the Court.

Respondent No.2 has filed an affidavit stating that at the intervention of elders, relatives and well-wishers, they have settled the issue and she is living with her husband happily by NC:
2024:KHC-K:8412 forgetting the past incident and restoring the marital obligations.
7.
An application under Section 359 r/w 528 of BNSS is filed seeking permission to compound the offences.

8. The Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S. Joshi and others v. State of Haryana and another, reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, has held that High Court in exercise of its inherent powers can quash criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint and Section 320 of the Code does not limit or affect the powers under Section 482 of the Code (528 of BNSS, 2023).
9.

In Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Hon'ble Apex Court, at para 58 has held as under:
"58.

entities.text: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another, reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Where the High Court quashes a criminal proceeding having regard to the fact that the dispute between the offender and the victim has been settled although the offences are not NC: 2024:KHC-K:8412 compoundable, it does so as in its opinion,
continuation of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and justice in the case demands that the dispute between the parties is put to an end and peace is restored; securing the ends of justice being the ultimate guiding factor.

No doubt,
crimes are acts which have harmful effect on the public and consist in wrongdoing that seriously endangers and threatens the well-being of the society and it is not safe to leave the crime-doer only because he and the victim have settled the dispute Thakru S/O Pooru Jadhav And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147501223/
4 amicably or that the victim has been paid compensation, yet certain crimes have been made compoundable in law, with or without the permission of the court.

entities.text: Pooru Jadhav And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In respect of serious offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc., or other offences of mental depravity under IPC or offences of moral turpitude under special statutes, like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity, the settlement between the offender and the victim can have no legal sanction at all.

However, certain offences which overwhelmingly and predominantly bear civil flavour having arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, financial,
partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony,
particularly relating to dowry, etc. or the family dispute, where the wrong NC:
2024:KHC-K:8412 is basically to the victim and the offender and the victim have settled all disputes between them amicably, irrespective of the fact that such offences have not been made compoundable, the High Court may within the framework of its inherent power, quash the criminal proceeding or criminal complaint or FIR if it is satisfied that on the face of such settlement, there is hardly any likelihood of the offender being convicted and by not quashing the criminal proceedings, justice shall be casualty and ends of justice shall be defeated.
The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive.
Each case will depend on its own facts and no hard-and-fast category can be prescribed."
10. This case arises out of a matrimonial dispute.
Respondent No.2/defacto complainant has submitted that the dispute has been settled and she is living with her husband happily.
This Court is satisfied that there is a genuine settlement between the parties and therefore, continuation of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility.
Hence to secure the ends of justice, it is just and proper to quash the proceedings pending against the petitioners.

Accordingly, the following:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:8412 ORDER Petitions are Allowed.
The entire proceedings pending against petitioners in C.C.No.20331/2022 on the file of the Court of I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kalaburagi are hereby quashed.
I.A.No.1/2024 is allowed.
